key_insight: Synthetic crystal structures can support diffusion pretraining for materials property prediction while reducing dependence on costly DFT-relaxed structures.
engineering_relevance: Fast machine-learned interatomic potentials enable larger, more structurally diverse pretraining datasets without requiring a new DFT relaxation for every generated crystal.
method: Generate structures through perturb-and-relax, MatterGen sampling, and protostructure enumeration.
Use machine-learned interatomic potentials where structural relaxation is required.
Compare coordinate denoising with continuous-time VP and sub-VP diffusion using a randomly initialized Orb-v2 backbone.
evidence_signal: Every synthetic-pretraining condition numerically beats random initialization across seven MatBench tasks; scaling protostructures from 20k to 165k matches or exceeds MP-20k pretraining on most tasks in an eight-task scaling study.
watch_item: The fixed 400-epoch scaling protocol increases both data diversity and optimization updates, so gains cannot be attributed to dataset size alone.
paper_title: Synthetic Crystal Data Generation for Diffusion Pretraining in Material Property Prediction
